newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Australia wine producers aim to boost exports.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Australia wine producers aim to boost exports.

text.p: The Australian wine industry on Thursday released a 1997-2001 five-year plan aiming to boost exports to 260 million litres worth A$896 million in the year 2001 from 130 million valued at A$471 million in 1996.
The plan, released by the Australian Wine Foundation at an industry conference here, also sees domestic wine sales growing to A$1.21 billion by 2001 from A$1.10 billion currently.
The plan is the first phase of the industry's Strategy 2025 which forecast a tripling in Australian wine annual sales to A$4.5 billion over the next 30 years from the current A$1.5 billion.
The thrust of the five year plan would be to accelerate penetration of international markets and initiate domestic market development, the plan said.

It would require increasing Australia's competitiveness through an upgrade of grape supply security and quality, further reduction in costs, a shift in investment priority from vineyards to processing and storage, and an improvement in government support, the plan said.
Winegrape supply was projected to reach almost one million tonnes by 2001 with premium varietals showing the strongest growth, rising to 733,000 tonnes in 2001 from 495,000 in 1996.
"Wineries will benefit from lower costs as the 'shortage premium' built into grape crisis over recent years is deminished," the plan said.
"Prices for grapes will reflect the underlying market demand for the processed product based on quality, consistency and variety," it said.

The plan said that following the record 1996 vintage, winery processing and storage capacity was currently fully utilised and substantial investment would be needed to process and store anticipated supplies for the 1997 vintage onwards.

The plan also urged improving government policy support, including certainty in retention of the current taxation level and structure for wine and brandy, reviewing trading stock valuations, and increased support for research and development.
